clue.text: Able to play at night till food is dished up

indicators.note: food that is dished up is served out, so these letters are laid out afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: A diner happy to keep going after dark as long as the meal arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is dished up' looks like the food being served; 'dished up' is the anagram signal working on TILL FOOD.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports ground lit by powerful lamps lets matches continue after darkness falls.

clue.text: Slangily brilliant about acting — poor at audition

indicators.note: about means the slang word goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: def is hip-hop slang meaning excellent
A is a standard abbreviation for acting, as in an acting manager

explanation.surface: A slangy rave review of a performer who then does badly at the tryout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audition' here means the act of hearing, not a tryout for actors.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who hears poorly has impaired hearing, which is what the word describes.

clue.text: What has me swallowing drink, upset? A mystery

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the combined letters are turned upside down, read backwards
swallowing means one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: taken as written
gin is a spirit, a common drink

explanation.surface: Someone puzzled at being made to gulp an upsetting drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowing' gives MGINE and 'upset' turns it to ENIGM; 'What has' is padding, and the clue's own A ends the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzling or inexplicable thing is a riddle, which is what the word names.

clue.text: Obscure words on dust-jacket cut short

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter is lopped off the word

parts.note: a blurb is the promotional text printed on a book's jacket

explanation.surface: Unclear text on a book cover, trimmed too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' removes the final B from BLURB.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something indistinct or hazy is to smear its outline, a verb sense of the word.

clue.text: Plot to get an easy situation

explanation.surface: A gardener's plot that turns out to be a cushy number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden plot planted with rose bushes is literally one; idiomatically the phrase means a comfortable, trouble-free state of life.

clue.text: Dog caught by Oliver

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
Ollie is a short form of the name Oliver

explanation.surface: A stray dog grabbed by a man called Oliver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' sets C beside OLLIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheepdog breed from Scotland, so an example of a dog.

clue.text: One who helps to govern town and realm, possibly

definitions.text: One who helps to govern town

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A civic official governing both town and wider realm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges AND REALM.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior member of a local council in English boroughs, so a civic official.

clue.text: Most of illness and decay restricting one that's hapless

indicators.note: most of means all but the last letter of the word is kept

parts.note: a malady is an illness

indicators.note: restricting means the word for decay hems in the numeral

parts.note: rot is decay
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone unlucky, beset by sickness and decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' leaves MALAD and 'restricting' makes ROIT; the surface reads 'hapless' as unlucky, but here it means inept.
explanation.definitionFit: Clumsy or bungling, which fits the sense of ineffectual and inept.

clue.text: To keep out of view is common after deception

indicators.note: after places the word for common following the word for deception

parts.note: a lie is a deception
low means vulgar or common

explanation.surface: Hiding away is a vulgar habit that follows lying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning to stay hidden or unnoticed for a while.

clue.text: Lights not working almost entirely

parts.note: a machine that is off is not working

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: all means entirely

explanation.surface: The lamps have failed, nearly all of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lights' are animal lungs, sold as butcher's meat; 'almost' trims ALL to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lungs of slaughtered animals are part of the edible innards sold by butchers.

clue.text: Storm about wanton orgy (an unpleasant sight)

indicators.note: about means the storm word goes round the rearranged letters

parts.note: a gale is a storm

indicators.note: wanton means unrestrained, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A tempest rages around a debauched party, an ugly scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanton' makes RGOY and 'about' wraps the storm word round it; the brackets hold the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotesque carved stone figure on a building is an ugly thing to look at.

clue.text: Try vainly to sell an animal that's gone'?

definitions.text: to sell an animal that's gone'?

explanation.surface: Hopeless salesmanship of a deceased beast.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes 'flog' as 'sell' (British slang) rather than 'whip'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to waste effort on a lost cause; literally it describes trying to sell a dead steed.

clue.text: One outburst of horseplay turns up among various rogues fond of company

indicators.note: among means the reversed piece sits inside the rearranged letters
various signals the letters appear in a different order
in a down clue, turns up means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a rag is a boisterous student prank

explanation.surface: A single prank breaks out among a crowd of rascals who enjoy each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' makes GARI and 'various' gives the shuffled rogues, which GARI sits 'among'; a rag is a British student prank.
explanation.definitionFit: Sociable people seek others out and enjoy group life.

clue.text: No real shock in extract from musical?

indicators.note: from places the word for extract after the name of the show

parts.note: Hair is a 1960s rock musical
a piece is an extract

explanation.surface: A scene excerpted from a show that turns out not to be shocking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' means a mass of hair, not a surprise: a wig is a false shock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A wig or toupee is false hair, so not a genuine mop.

clue.text: Shaking with some secret remorse

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Trembling with hidden guilt.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiver or vibration is a shaking movement; the noun stands for the act.

clue.text: More than one team losing heart cheers a period of rest

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle letter of the word is taken out

parts.note: sides are teams
ta is British informal thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: Dispirited teams give thanks for a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' removes D from SIDES.
explanation.definitionFit: An afternoon nap, especially in hot countries, is a break for sleeping.

clue.text: Abandoning position? A Petty Officer has to remain round prow of ship

parts.note: PO is the naval abbreviation for petty officer

indicators.note: round means the verb for remain goes around that letter

parts.note: to stay is to remain

indicators.note: the prow is the front of a ship, so its first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A naval officer must stay near the bow rather than desert his post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'position' means a stance or belief, not a station on board.
explanation.definitionFit: Renouncing one's faith or principles is forsaking a stance once held.

clue.text: It's got a sprint running with a bit of loudness!

definitions.text: It's got a sprint running with a bit of loudness!

indicators.note: running suggests the letters are set loose and rearranged
a bit of means only the first letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: Describes the bang that starts a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' rearranges ITS GOT A SPRINT and 'a bit of' adds L from loudness; the whole clue also describes the gun.
explanation.definitionFit: The gun fired to start a race sets sprinters going with a bang.

clue.text: Information brought up about man's country in Scandinavia…

indicators.note: about means the reversed word goes round the name
in a down clue, brought up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: news is information
Ed is a man's name; the 's reads as 'is', a link

explanation.surface: Reports about a man's homeland in the far north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reverses NEWS to SWEN, which goes 'about' ED.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nordic kingdom bordering Norway and Finland, so one of the Scandinavian states.

clue.text: … no way one's cold in Scandinavia

parts.note: Rd is the abbreviation for road, a way
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Denying that anyone feels chilly up north.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to the clue above but adds nothing to the parse.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the northern European region including Scandinavia.

clue.text: Annoying person with not long to live?

explanation.surface: A pest whose days are numbered.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a pest or a cheeky child; read literally it is one about to die.

clue.text: Cover skin

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to conceal; as a noun it is an animal's pelt.

clue.text: Rowing crew shows strength, though losing first member

indicators.note: losing first member means the opening letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: weight means force or influence, strength

explanation.surface: A boat team shows its power even after losing its first oarsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' sounds like a crew member but means a letter of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing boat with eight oarsmen is named for its number of rowers.

clue.text: Fielder drops fifth, the sap

indicators.note: drops fifth means the fifth letter of the word is removed

parts.note: gully is a cricket fielding position, and the fielder there

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder spills a catch off the fifth ball and is called a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops' suggests a dropped catch; GULLY is a fielding position near the slips in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A dupe, someone easily fooled, is a sucker or sap.

clue.text: Community invested in source of money that's productive

indicators.note: invested in means the abbreviation is placed inside the money word

parts.note: a fund is a source of money
EC is the European Community

explanation.surface: A community puts money into a fund that pays off.
explanation.definitionFit: Fertile and fruitful, yielding a lot.

clue.text: I'm embracing wanton ladies (an implausible belief)

indicators.note: embracing means the first piece holds the rearranged letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: wanton means unrestrained, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone hugging loose women while holding naive views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanton' rearranges LADIES to DEALIS, held by IM.
explanation.definitionFit: Pursuit of lofty ideals often seen as unrealistic is the sense here.
